class: UNRESOLVED — AND THIS ARCHIVE GOT IT WRONG THREE TIMES IN ONE EVENING
verdict: THE INSTRUMENT IS REAL AND NOBODY HAS READ IT. Find a Will answers in two halves. The DIGITAL half holds only grants from 1996, so a 1973 query returns 0 before anything is searched — that is the zero the original negative was built on. The IMAGE half calls an OCR endpoint, pp_cowindex_default_search, over the calendar split into chunks named for the first surname on each. CALLED DIRECTLY IT PLAINLY WORKS: WEAR 1973 → 41 chunks, SMITH 1973 → 469, LUWINSKI → 0, ZQXVWYRK → 0. Two chunks bracket the name: 009223_weake_1973.pdf (weake–weare) and 009225_wearmouth_1973.pdf (wearmouth–weatherby). NEITHER HAS BEEN OPENED. *** AND THE THREE WRONG ANSWERS, KEPT BECAUSE THEY ARE THE USEFUL PART. *** (1) The original read the digital zero as an answer about 1973. (2) The first re-run called the instrument OCR-over-images and cited a Zqxvwyrk control returning 0 and 0 — run down a path where the year never reached the form, and published without being repeated. (3) The second re-run corrected that to “no search at all” on the strength of the page printing “41 document pages returned” for Wear, Smith, Luwinski, nonsense, 1979, a forename and the keyword AUBREY alike. THAT DISPLAYED COUNT IS A DEFECT IN THE SERVICE'S OWN PAGE. THE COMMON FAULT IN ALL THREE IS READING THE RENDERED PAGE INSTEAD OF THE REQUEST UNDERNEATH IT, and all three dissolve the moment the endpoint is called directly and the counts move with the surname.
